subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate the Codex app-server 10-second external-auth refresh callback in its own bridge now, and if so should the default behavior return usable cached tokens instead of force-refreshing every callback?
rationale: The code path crosses OpenClaw OAuth ownership, provider auth recovery, runtime deadlines, and upstream Codex protocol behavior; automation should not pick the permanent auth contract or timeout budgets without owner intent.

options.title: Mitigate in OpenClaw bridge
options.body: Return still-usable cached OAuth tokens for app-server refresh callbacks and spend the 10-second budget only when a real refresh is required, with status/error tests and a packaged OAuth smoke.

options.title: Land broader auth deadline work first
options.body: Prioritize https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93952 for deadlock recovery, then re-test this exact callback timeout before changing the force-refresh contract.

options.title: Wait for upstream configurability
options.body: Keep OpenClaw behavior unchanged and rely on openai/codex timeout configurability, accepting continued failures on current shipped runtimes until that dependency is updated.

recommendation.title: Mitigate in OpenClaw bridge
recommendation.body: Return still-usable cached OAuth tokens for app-server refresh callbacks and spend the 10-second budget only when a real refresh is required, with status/error tests and a packaged OAuth smoke.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent auth/security and Codex app-server history makes this the strongest owner signal for the cross-boundary timeout and credential-handling decision.
